newsitem.title: UK: MGAM /IMRO agree terms for investors.
newsitem.headline: MGAM /IMRO agree terms for investors.

text.p: Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), part of Germany's Deutsche Bank, and British investment management regulator IMRO said on Friday they had agreed the basis of compensation for investors in three European funds.

Trading in the funds was suspended in September following the discovery of irregularities in their valuations. MGAM fund manager Peter Young was later sacked by the firm and is under investigation by Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO).

"We are pleased that these discussions have been brought to a speedy conclusion. It is in the interests of investors that compensation will be paid without undue delay," Daniel Waters of the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) said in a statement, adding the agreement was fair and equitable.

The Morgan Grenfell European Growth Trust, Morgan Grenfell Europa Fund and Morgan Grenfell European Capital Growth Fund, which were held by some 90,000 retail investors, resumed trading after a 180 million pound ($299.9 million) cash-injection by Deutsche, which said it would compensate for any losses.

IMRO and MGAM said in separate statements that all investors in these funds at any time between August 1 1995 and September 5 1996 would be considered for compensation. Deutsche Bank said it expected to pay about 200 million pounds although it was too early to specify the exact cost.

Compensation would be "the difference between the investment return from the fund and the return provided by a specially compiled index of comparable funds" IMRO said, adding that Morgan Grenfell would also be paying interest on the payments.

MGAM chief executive Robert Smith, who was appointed after four MGAM directors were purged from the firm in October, said all investors would be "compensated at least to the level of their original investment, which means no one will lose money as a result of these events".
